document.title: Let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
document.summary: Adds Host Control: a Vita links to a computer's Host Companion, Deck Apps call its built-in and custom plugins, and computers can push events to Deck Apps.
document.why: [PR #144](source:s1) says a Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it.

sources.label: PR #144
sources.title: feat(host-control): let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins

sources.label: chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #144
sources.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
sources.body: Reject unauthorized peers before reading their bodies. When a non-linked LAN peer sends a slow or concurrent request, `reply` waits for `readBody` to finish before checking `isAllowed`; `readBody` continues consuming the stream and buffers up to 64 KiB per request, so denied peers can tie up sockets and memory before receiving a 403. Check the peer before reading the body, or abort unauthorized requests immediately, so the allowlist also protects availability.

sources.label: cursor[bot] on PR #144
sources.author: cursor[bot]
sources.body: Risk: high. This adds a LAN HTTP listener, persisted host links, and a new SDK/companion contract, so it is above the medium approval threshold and was not approved. Cursor Bugbot was skipped and no Security Agent check ran; human review is needed and no reviewers were assigned.

sources.title: Host Control slice A: wire contract and SDK client
Host Control slice B: Host Companion CLI
Host Control slice C: native link listener and Shell Host Control screen

lookFor: [#109](source:s6) asks for flat commands that authors call but do not define. At head authors define `defineHostPlugin` plugins, and the wire request gains a `plugin` field. [PR #144](source:s1) lists the plugins as a deviation.
[#109](source:s6) asks for `HostCapabilities.commands` as a `string[]`. At head `capabilities` returns `plugins`, each with its own `commands`. No source gives a reason.

[#109](source:s6) has the default `host` read `nativeGetHostControlUrl()`. At head the client reads `nativeGetHostControlLinks()`, a JSON array, and calls take a `hostId`. [PR #144](source:s1) lists the array as a deviation.
[#110](source:s7) puts an `enable` list in the config, which would keep computer-acting commands off until named. At head `config.ts` has no `enable` field, and no source gives a reason.
[#110](source:s7) keeps one `vita` address in the config. At head the config holds a `vitas` list, and no source gives a reason.

[#111](source:s8) binds the link listener on 8798, and its Shell screen shows `Link address: 192.168.1.177:8798`. At head the LAN Listener binds 8787 and falls forward, and the screen shows the `vitadeck-host-companion link` command with its address. [PR #144](source:s1) says links share that listener after testing.
[#111](source:s8) stops the listener when a link succeeds, on Circle, and on Start. At head only the Shell Listener Entry or VitaDeck's exit stops it, so Circle and Start leave it running.

[#111](source:s8) keeps one link in `host-control-link.json`, and forgetting it deletes the file. At head the store keeps up to four links in `host-control-links.json`, and forgetting one leaves the rest. [PR #144](source:s1) lists several links as a deviation.
[#111](source:s8) makes `POST /link` the only route on the link listener. At head `/link` shares port 8787 with `POST /upload` and `GET /`.

[PR #144](source:s1) says Codex flagged the companion devDependency as unpublished, and declined the fix as a release decision. At head `copy-templates` still pins `@vitadeck/host-companion` to `^0.1.0`, which is not on npm.

The review bot on the PR says human review is needed and no reviewers were assigned ([cursor[bot]](source:s5)). [PR #144](source:s1) says three review loops ran, each with Claude and Muse, and names no human reviewer.

groups.title: LAN Listener serves uploads, links
groups.why: After testing, the separate link listener felt clunky, [PR #144](source:s1) says, so links share the always-on LAN Listener.
groups.summary: The upload server becomes the LAN Listener, which also answers `POST /link` and starts at boot. Its request parsing and JSON replies move into `net/http.c`.

attention.note: The listener runs from boot, and `POST /link` and `POST /upload` answer any LAN peer. `handler_thread` picks the route from the request line, and nothing checks the peer or a credential first. A peer can add a link or install a Deck App whenever VitaDeck runs, which ADR 0004 accepts until credentials exist.

focus.caption: Relink or save; any non-200 reply is rejected.

notes.body: The request line alone picks the route, so `handle_link` runs with no peer check.

fileNotes.src/net/http.c: Request reading, response writing and the JSON error body, moved from `upload/http_server.c`.
fileNotes.src/net/http.h: Declares the helpers both routes use; the body cap comes from the caller.
fileNotes.src/platform/lan_address.h: Declares the IPv4 address the listener shows.

groups.title: SDK client calls computers
groups.summary: `createHostClient` posts each command to a computer's `/command` and resolves every failure as a coded `HostResult`. `linkedHosts` reads the Shell's links on each call.

attention.note: A command still running at 5 s resolves `timeout`, but the Vita's `fetch` has no abort, so the computer may still run it. The client never retries, so a caller cannot tell whether the command ran.

focus.caption: The race returns at the timeout; the fetch keeps running.

Posts to `{url}command`, races a 5 s timer, and maps network, JSON and status failures to coded results.

groups.title: Companion answers linked peers
groups.summary: `startHostCompanion` serves `POST /command`, checks the peer before reading the body, as [a Codex review](source:s2) asked, and routes to a loaded plugin.

attention.note: Until a Vita links, `isAllowed` returns true for every peer, and `start` listens on `0.0.0.0`. Any LAN peer can then call every loaded command, including installed plugins, which run with the user's permissions. Once a link exists, only that Vita's address, loopback and this computer's own addresses get answers.

questions: Why does `isAllowed` admit every peer until a Vita links, instead of refusing?

focus.caption: The peer check runs first; an unlinked peer gets 403.

notes.body: With no linked Vita, this admits every peer, so any LAN peer gets answers.

groups.title: Companion loads and installs packages
groups.summary: `start` loads each installed package by file URL and reloads it on change; `install` stages an archive, then renames it into `plugins/`.

attention.note: A package loads when `manifest.json` has `schemaVersion` 1 and its default export has an `id` and a `Map` of commands. The loader checks that shape rather than the SDK's classes, so a companion built from another SDK version still loads the package and matches `HostCommandError` by name and code.

focus.caption: The import query is a content hash, so rebuilds load fresh.

groups.title: Event log and held wait
groups.summary: `core.events` answers at once with newer events, or holds the request for the plugin's next event for up to 25 s.

attention.note: The log keeps 100 events per plugin and drops the oldest. A wait returns only what is kept while `next` still moves on, so a Deck App more than 100 events behind gets no sign of the gap.

focus.caption: A held wait wakes on the next emit or the timer.

fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/events.ts: Numbers events, keeps the last 100 per plugin, and holds waits until a plugin emits or the timer ends.
fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/core.ts: `events` rejects an unloaded plugin with `unknown_plugin`, then hands the wait to the log.
fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/server.ts: Gates each lifecycle's `emit` on its own running flag, so a stopped plugin's emits drop.
fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/test/server.t: Covers the held wait, a reset after restart, and `close` answering waits.

groups.title: Deck App watches events
groups.summary: `watchHostEvents` keeps one `core.events` wait open and passes each batch's `next` as `after`.

attention.note: A throw from `onEvent` rejects the `wait` that `void wait()` starts, and nothing catches that rejection, so the Deck App fails. The doc comment on `watchHostEvents` says a throw fails the Deck App.

focus.caption: A throw from `onEvent` here rejects the wait.

Adds `watchHostEvents`, a loop of `core.events` waits that starts with no `after` and then passes `next`.
fileNotes.js/packages/sdk/test/host-control.test.t: Covers the `after` sequence of a watch and stopping from inside a callback.

groups.title: Stop cancels pending fetches
groups.summary: Stopping a Deck App cancels its pending fetches at curl's next progress call, so a held event wait does not hold up the stop.

fileNotes.src/jslib/fetch.c: Adds a `cancelled` flag to each request, which `fetch_shutdown` sets on every pending one before joining.
fileNotes.tests/js_limits_harness.c: Stops a runtime whose fetch waits on a silent server, and fails if the stop takes over 3 s.

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): relink attempts run one at a time and re-read the config
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Retries for different Vitas ran on independent timers, and each save
wrote the same temporary file from a config read before the request.
All attempts now share one queue, a failure is logged, and linkVita
reads the config again just before changing its Vitas. Also list
unknown_link with the other link endpoint codes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): the companion relinks its Vitas on every start
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A new computer IP or companion port broke commands until the user ran
`link` again. `start` now re-sends the link to every Vita in its config
with `relink: true`, which VitaDeck applies only to a link it still has,
so a computer forgotten in the Shell is not linked back: VitaDeck
answers 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita
that does not answer is retried every 30 s. The host-control demo asks
for capabilities again when a relink changes the URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(shell): one LAN Listener for upload and link, on from startup
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Setting up a Deck App with a Host Control Plugin needed two Shell steps
and two addresses: start Upload for `vitadeck dev`, then open Host
Control for `link`. The upload server now also serves `POST /link`,
VitaDeck starts it at boot, and the Shell row turns it off and on. Both
CLIs take the same Vita address (port 8787).

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): start plugin lifecycles after binding the port
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A busy port no longer leaves a plugin's timers running. Stopping twice is a
no-op, each plugin keeps its own 100 events, and core.events answers
unknown_plugin for a plugin the companion has not loaded. The SDK says a
throw from a watch callback stops watching.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): computers push events to Deck Apps by long-polling
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A plugin declares Host Control Events next to its commands and emits them
from a start(emit) lifecycle the companion runs while it is loaded. The
companion numbers recent events, and core.events holds a request until the
plugin's next event or 25 s. watchHostEvents in the SDK keeps one such
request open, so an event reaches the Vita within one round trip. core.notify
and `vitadeck-host-companion notify` let any script send a notice, which the
host-control demo shows.

Stopping a Deck App now cancels its pending fetches through curl's progress
callback, so a held request no longer stalls a reload or shutdown.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: docs(skills): add vitadeck-host-control and cover Host Control in the others
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The new public skill covers running and linking the Host Companion, calling
plugins from a Deck App, writing plugins with a Deck App or standalone, the
author loop, installing .vdplugin packages, and error codes. deck-app-init
learns --host-plugin and --host-plugin-only, manual-testing gets a Host
Control section, vdapp-upload says .vdplugin.zip goes to the computer, and
build lists the companion bundle.

commits.subject: feat(sdk): Host Plugins can be authored without a Deck App
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A vitadeck.config.json may have hostPlugin without an entry: build then
writes only the .vdplugin package and zip, and dev rebuilds them without a
Runtime Upload URL. `vitadeck create <name> --host-plugin-only` scaffolds such
a project, whose package.json exports host/plugin.ts so any Deck App can
depend on it. Template package.json files all get published versions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(host-control): a broken plugin build keeps the last good package
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Bundle before replacing the package folder, copy linked files as files, and
require hostPlugin.files to be a folder. The companion ignores __MACOSX/ in
archives and points a --plugin .zip at install. Docs say the zip keeps no
file modes and that files/ is read per call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): a Deck App's plugin ships as a .vdplugin package and zip
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion
installs archives or folders into ~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin, loads the
entry by file URL so it finds its files through import.meta.url, and watches
package folders recursively.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): load plugins from file copies, resolve paths from the cwd
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A bundled CommonJS dependency calls createRequire(import.meta.url), which a
data: URL cannot satisfy; plugins now load from a content-hashed .mjs copy.
Paths resolve against the working directory except under the repo's own
`host-companion` script, so a Deck App's `host` script works from anywhere.
Plugin ids may start with a digit, and watcher errors are logged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): built-in plugins, .vdplugin files, vitadeck-host-companion
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App now keeps its own Host Control Plugin in its project: `hostPlugin`
in vitadeck.config.json makes `vitadeck build` bundle the implementation into
one self-contained <slug>.vdplugin, and `vitadeck create --host-plugin`
scaffolds it. Users install that file with `vitadeck-host-companion install`;
the companion reloads installed and --plugin files when they change.

systemStats moves into the companion as a built-in, with its registry in
@vitadeck/sdk/host-control next to implementHostPlugin and HostCommandError.
The companion is a dependency-free bundled package with the
vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): Host Control Link listener, store, getter, and Shell screen
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Slice C of ADR 0004. VitaDeck keeps up to four Host Control Links in <data root>/host-control-links.json and exposes them to Deck Apps through nativeGetHostControlLinks. The Shell Host Control Screen starts a listener on 8798-8807 that accepts one POST /link, and Cross forgets a linked computer.

Upload's HTTP helpers move to src/net/http, LAN address detection to src/platform/lan_address_*, jimp's implementation and the JSON skip and escape helpers to src/core/json, and Deck App Storage's Vita-safe file replace to src/core/util so the link store reuses it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
